stem: Two settlements face the same flood depth. One has elevated homes and evacuation support; the other has fragile ground-level homes and no assistance. Why may their disaster risk differ?

choices.text: Different hazard intensity
Different population totals
Differing vulnerability and capacity
Differing greenhouse-gas emissions

explanation: RA 10121 Section 3(m) defines potential disaster losses; Sections 3(ii) and 3(b) address assessment of hazards, exposure, vulnerability and coping capacities. stem: A planner claims sea-level rise at a location can be assessed solely from global ocean warming, ignoring sinking land. Which correction matches the Act's definition?

Attribute the full local rise to ocean expansion.
Use subsidence measurements instead of ocean-level data.
Include local subsidence alongside global influences.

stem: An accused was arraigned, duly notified of trial and then absent without justification. Does Article III categorically prohibit trial from proceeding because of that absence?

stem: A disaster-risk review distinguishes I: reducing structural vulnerability, II: developing ability to act on warnings, and III: restoring disrupted services after impact. Project A reinforces a bridge without changing the storm forecast; B teaches households how to interpret a warning and rehearse a route; C restores a damaged water line. Which mapping and limitation are justified under RA 10121?

choices.text: A addresses I, B addresses II and C addresses III; changing vulnerability need not change the storm hazard.
A addresses I, B addresses III and C addresses II; changing vulnerability need not change the storm hazard.
A addresses II, B addresses I and C addresses III; restoring the water line establishes pre-impact preparedness.
A addresses I, B addresses II and C addresses III; unchanged storm intensity means A has not reduced disaster risk.

explanation: Reinforcement mitigates structural impacts, warning interpretation and rehearsal build preparedness, and post-impact restoration is rehabilitation. Hazard intensity and vulnerability are distinct: unchanged storm intensity does not show unchanged risk. Two alternatives have the same correct mapping, requiring evaluation of the limitation as well.

stem: A town compares two disaster-risk proposals. In K, residents attend a presentation but cannot influence assessment or remedy selection; radio numbers are its only readiness measure. In L, residents identify risks, choose remedies and monitor implementation; its evaluation also tests whether messages are understood and evacuation actions can be performed. Which paired assessment best applies community-based DRRM and early-warning definitions?

choices.text: K meets both definitions; L adds voluntary response checks.
K lacks participation; its radios establish response capacity.
K lacks both; L addresses participation and response capacity.
K and L meet participation requirements; only L checks response.

explanation: Section 3(e) requires active community roles, not attendance alone; Section 3(q) requires understanding and capacity to respond, not an equipment inventory alone. K establishes neither dimension. L's participation and functional checks address both; the alternatives incorrectly treat attendance or radio numbers as sufficient.

stem: A climate review considers K: elevated storage powered by higher-emission generators; L: lower-emission power with unchanged flood exposure; M: lower-emission power plus flood-safe storage. The reviewer distinguishes an action's adaptation purpose from its emissions effect and from meeting both objectives. Which assessment keeps all three distinctions?

choices.text: K adapts, L mitigates and M does both; K's adaptation also establishes emissions reduction.
K mitigates, L adapts and M does both; L's emissions changes do not relocate exposed stores.
K adapts, L mitigates and M does both; combining the two makes their meanings interchangeable.
K adapts, L mitigates and M does both; K's higher emissions do not erase its adaptation role.

explanation: Adaptation addresses climatic impacts, while mitigation addresses greenhouse-gas sources and sinks. K adapts despite higher emissions; L mitigates without the flood-storage remedy; M combines the two. Combining them does not merge their definitions, and exposure reduction alone does not prove emissions reduction.

stem: Office P uses climate analysis during project design but omits it from later sector decisions. Office Q involves women and men in implementation but not design, monitoring or evaluation. Office R integrates climate measures into relevant planning and sector decisions and gender concerns through design, implementation, monitoring and evaluation. Which comparison best fits the two mainstreaming definitions in RA 9729?

choices.text: P and Q each show partial integration; R addresses both definitions.
P fully integrates climate measures; Q is partial; R addresses both definitions.
P is partial; Q fully integrates gender concerns; R addresses both definitions.
P and Q are partial; R's later-stage work replaces gender concerns during design.

explanation: Section 3(m) integrates climate measures into development planning and sector decisions. Section 3(i) integrates gender concerns through design, implementation, monitoring and evaluation. P and Q each omit required dimensions; R explicitly addresses both. Later-stage gender work does not replace design participation.

stem: During custodial investigation, Leo signs a waiver without counsel, while Neri gives an unwritten waiver with counsel present. Officers use physical coercion on both. Which combined assessment follows Article III, Section 12?

choices.text: Leo's writing validates his waiver, but Neri's lack of writing invalidates hers; coercion remains prohibited
Neither waiver meets both requirements, and counsel's presence or a signature does not authorize coercion
Both waivers are valid because each satisfies one safeguard; coercion remains prohibited
Neither waiver meets both requirements, but a valid waiver would authorize physical coercion

explanation: Section 12(1) requires writing and counsel together; each waiver lacks one. Section 12(2) independently forbids coercion. Knowing only the waiver rule leaves two plausible alternatives; the separate coercion safeguard resolves them.

stem: Accused J was arraigned, duly notified and unjustifiably absent. Accused K was notified but has not yet been arraigned. A court says both absences prove guilt and allow the same trial-in-absence exception. Which review is best under Article III, Section 14(2)?

choices.text: J and K meet the exception; neither absence establishes guilt.
Only J meets the exception; J's absence establishes guilt.
Only J meets the exception; neither absence establishes guilt.
Neither meets the exception; J still needs written consent to an absent trial.

explanation: Article III, Section 14(2) requires arraignment, due notice and unjustifiable absence; only J meets the supplied conditions. Neither absence by itself establishes guilt. The exception does not depend on written consent and does not replace the presumption of innocence.

stem: A covered employee files a statement showing assets and debts but omits a business interest. She also proposes using classified office data to help a bidder without accepting payment. Which analysis correctly separates Sections 7(c) and 8?

choices.text: The SALN is incomplete; unpaid disclosure is permissible.
The SALN is complete if net worth is right; disclosure is prohibited.
The SALN is complete if net worth is right; unpaid disclosure is permissible.
The SALN is incomplete; conferring undue advantage is prohibited despite no payment.

explanation: Section 8 requires business interests as well as assets, liabilities and net worth, so the statement is incomplete. Section 7(c) prohibits the proposed conferral of undue advantage using nonpublic official information without requiring personal payment. Neither correct net worth nor absence of fees cures these defects.

stem: A professional leaves an agency and, six months later, plans private work on an unrelated matter outside that agency. A separate proposed assignment is a professional matter before the former agency. Assume no other restriction or conflict applies. Which assessment matches Section 7(b)'s post-separation exception?

choices.text: Unrelated practice is excepted; the former-agency matter remains barred for one year.
Both are barred; the one-year continuation covers all private professional practice.
Only unrelated practice is barred; the former-agency matter falls within the exception.
Both are excepted; separation also ends the bar for matters before the former agency.

explanation: Section 7(b)'s post-separation paragraph excepts general private professional practice from the one-year continuation but retains the bar for a professional matter before the former agency. The unrelated work is therefore excepted under the stated no-other-restriction assumption; the former-agency matter remains barred at six months.
